title: Cheaper state reads: one gated cross-attention write per token instead of the full cell
follows: R1.03 (PARTIAL: memory works, read is expensive), R1.01 lesson 5 (9x FLOPs at equal parameters)
question: Does replacing the per-token cell (O(M d^2)) by a gated cross-attention write (O(d^2 + M d)) keep rouge-mem's capability and recall while cutting inference FLOPs to <= 1/3?

predictions.C1-C3: gating as written in the gate; C4 (within 1.5x of the Transformer's FLOPs) is reported
predictions.local_measurement: untrained: rouge-mem 96.9 MFLOP/example, rouge-cheap 15.6 MFLOP (d 104; 6.2x fewer), Transformer 22.8 MFLOP
predictions.params: rouge-cheap d=104 (~221k) to stay parameter-matched with rouge-mem (218k)

prior_art: Perceiver cross-attention reads (2107.14795), gated RNN updates, linear-attention writes (2006.16236)
not_claimed: All mechanisms are prior art (see docs/rouge/research/prior-art.md); only the measurement is new.
